title: Israel's CropX buried sensors in the ground, and the fields got less water and more yield

trailer.text: CropX is an Israeli provider of advanced adaptive irrigation technology.
The company was founded by Isaac Bentwich, and its CEO, Tomer Tzach, was born in Israel.
Farmers themselves bury mushroom-like sensors in the ground, which collect moisture, salinity and temperature data and send it to the cloud.
According to the company, in a six-month pilot in Arizona the system saved 40% of the irrigation water.
Streamlining irrigation made it possible to grow an additional crop, and the revenue from the parcel rose by 10%.

glance.label: Scale
glance.value: Systems in 40 countries, as of the article

glance.label: Recognition
glance.value: The Israel Innovation Authority describes the solution

paragraphs.text: According to the article, some areas of the land are left swamped and others are left dehydrated.
Irrigation that does not distinguish between them yields smaller harvests, and can lead to chemical runoff that threatens aquatic life and the quality of drinking water.
According to Tzach, over-irrigation wastes water and hurts the crop.
Potatoes, for example, can rot from too much water.
According to Tzach, when you look at the field from above, the figures come too late.
It usually takes weeks before you see something on the plant's leaves.
According to Bentwich, only four percent of irrigated farms use Israeli drip irrigation, even though it improves yields and reduces costs.
According to the article, 85 percent of irrigated farms use pivot irrigation.

stations.title: A doctor in New Zealand, and a company in Israel

paragraphs.text: Isaac Bentwich is a doctor by training.
He began to understand the problem when his family stayed in New Zealand for two and a half years, during a world tour.
Bentwich founded CropX.
He was described as CEO of an Israeli agricultural analytics company.
According to Globes, he is no longer active in the company.
Tomer Tzach was born in Israel and grew up in the US.
He returned to Israel for military service, and was a transport pilot in the air force for seven years.
Later he joined CropX as CEO.
According to him, when he joined, the company did irrigation management only.
According to CropX's own website, the company was founded in 2013 in New Zealand.
CropX's technology is based on sensors planted in the soil at specific points in the field.
The sensors are mushroom-like, and farmers install them themselves.
An app guides farmers on where to place them.
Other companies sometimes require professional planting, which costs more.
The sensors measure moisture, salinity and temperature in the soil, at various depths.
According to the Government of South Australia, the sensor measures at depths of 20 and 46 centimetres.
The data passes wirelessly to the cloud, where a system collects and analyzes it.
One sensor can monitor a section of field of 20 to 80 dunams.
The sensors run on a battery, which can last up to four years.
The company generates irrigation maps, and automatically applies the right amount of water to each part of the field.
The products work with existing pivot systems, which would be costly for farmers to replace.
A new version of the sensor is screwed into the ground, and installation was shortened from 20 minutes to four.
CropX completed a pilot project in Arizona, in cooperation with the IAF investment company.
The trial lasted six months, on a round 500-dunam plot with a mobile irrigation system.
The company divided an alfalfa field into 20 equal portions.
Each portion was grown under different irrigation and fertilizing conditions.
According to the company, at the end of the trial it turned out that the system had saved 40% of the irrigation water.
The water saved was estimated at 190 million liters, equivalent to 76 Olympic swimming pools.
Streamlining irrigation made it possible to grow an additional crop during the pilot period, which yielded 10% more crops.
Revenue from the parcel rose from $280,000 to $310,000.
According to Tzach, when farmers are shown the data, they are surprised to discover that they did not irrigate and fertilize enough.
According to Globes, the technology saves 40% of irrigation water and increases crops by 10%.
According to ISRAEL21c, the system releases into the soil only the amounts that are needed.
Other sources give other figures.
In New Zealand, the dairy collective Dairy Holdings, which covers over 20,000 hectares, used CropX to reduce irrigation by 30%.
According to the article, the savings to farmers are at least three times the cost of using CropX.
The benefits are reaped within the first harvest.
The low price ranges between $4 and $18 per acre.

stations.title: From twenty farms to forty countries

paragraphs.text: According to TechCrunch, the technology was used at 20 row crop farms in four US states, encompassing some 5,000 acres.
According to the company's report, corn yields increased by up to 10 bushels per acre, using 30% less water.
Tzach said that in 2018 international sales began, for example in Australia.
The technology also expanded to Latin America and New Zealand.
As of the Globes article, the company had deployed 2,000 sensors, and its systems are deployed in 40 countries.
According to Tzach, municipalities in the US also use the product in water treatment facilities.
According to ISRAEL21c, CropX is in a partnership with NASA.
According to the article, with the normalization of relations between Israel and the UAE, the UAE is interested in adapting CropX.
According to Tzach, customers also asked for fertilizer management, crop protection, crop reporting and scouting, so the company decided to buy and integrate companies.
Seven acquisitions in five years turned CropX from a precision irrigation startup into a broad platform.
One of them was Tule Technologies, from which the evapotranspiration technology came.
According to the company's announcement, CropX is launching in Australasia a sensor that monitors the plants' water use in the field in real time through evapotranspiration.
The latest acquisition, of the Israeli company Acclym in September 2025, takes CropX into the field of sustainability reporting.
According to AgFunderNews, most customers are agribusinesses, such as dealers, retailers and processors.
Tzach is based in Israel, and according to him the company has offices around the world.
According to him, many sensors and computing capabilities will make it possible to assemble the world's largest database of soil data.
Future plans also include information for insurance companies that insure crops.
According to Globes, CropX raised $1.3 million in its seed round.
The investment round was extended from $9 million to $10 million to accommodate investor interest.
According to TechCrunch, Bosch and Flex added one million dollars to the round.
Investors include Innovation Endeavors, of former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and the Finistere Ventures fund.
GreenSoil and OurCrowd also participated in the round.
The strategic investment by ICL (Israel Chemicals) was its first investment in precise agriculture, and according to Tzach it is significant.
According to Tzach, CropX is extending its Series C mainly to fund additional acquisitions, rather than day-to-day operations.
The Israel Innovation Authority describes CropX as a cloud-based software solution with wireless sensors, which boosts crop yields and saves water and energy.
Tzach listed fundraising, market penetration and sales as challenges.
He noted that fixing hardware issues can take time.
According to Tzach, in its rush to acquire many companies CropX made mistakes, but has learned its lesson.
According to him, most of the acquired companies were profitable, and out of seven only one was in distress.

claims.quote: who is based in Israel but notes that CropX has offices around the world

claims.text: לדברי צח, חיישנים רבים ויכולות חישוב יאפשרו להרכיב את מאגר נתוני הקרקע הגדול בעולם.
claims.quote: make it possible to assemble the world's largest database of soil data

claims.text: תוכניות העתיד של החברה כוללות הרחבה למידע עבור חברות ביטוח שמבטחות יבולים.
claims.quote: Future plans include expansion to information for insurance companies that insure crops.

claims.text: לפי הכתבה, CropX גייסה 1.3 מיליון דולר בסבב הזרע ועוד 10 מיליון דולר בסבב A ביוני 2015.
claims.quote: CropX raised $1.3 million in its seed round and $10 million more in its Series A round in June 2015.

claims.text: סבב ההשקעה הורחב מ-9 ל-10 מיליון דולר כדי להיענות לעניין המשקיעים.
claims.quote: led the investment round, which was extended from $9 million to $10 million to accommodate investor interest.

claims.text: לפי טכקראנץ', בוש ופלקס הוסיפו מיליון דולר לסבב A, שהסתכם כעת ב-10 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: added $1 million in venture funding to the Series A round for CropX, which now totals $10 million.

claims.text: בין המשקיעים ב-CropX נמנים Innovation Endeavors של אריק שמידט, לשעבר מנכ"ל גוגל, וקרן Finistere Ventures.
claims.quote: Investors in CropX include former Google CEO Eric Schmidt's Innovation Endeavors; US venture capital fund Finistere Ventures

claims.text: לפי הכתבה, סבב A שנסגר ביוני הסתכם ב-9 מיליון דולר, ובו השתתפו גם GreenSoil ו-OurCrowd.
claims.quote: GreenSoil and OurCrowd also participated in the Series A fundraising round that closed in June at $9 million.

claims.text: השקעה אסטרטגית של איי.סי.אל (כימיקלים לישראל) במאי הייתה ההשקעה הראשונה שלה בחקלאות מדייקת, ולדברי צח היא משמעותית.
claims.quote: Israel Chemicals' first investment in precise agriculture. Tzach says that the investment is significant

claims.text: לדברי צח, CropX מרחיבה את סבב C בעיקר כדי לממן רכישות נוספות ולא פעילות שוטפת.
claims.quote: CropX is extending its Series C, mainly to fund additional acquisitions rather than day-to-day operations

claims.text: צח מנה כאתגרים גיוס כספים, חדירה לשוק ומכירות, וציין שתקלות חומרה עלולות לקחת זמן לתיקון.
claims.quote: Fundraising, market penetration and sales. Also our product is a mix of hardware and software, and hardware can be challenging because issues with hardware can take time to fix.

claims.text: לדברי צח, בחיפזון לרכוש חברות רבות CropX עשתה טעויות, אך למדה את הלקח.
claims.quote: CropX made mistakes during its rush to acquire so many companies in such a short space of time, says Tzach, but has learned its lesson.

claims.text: לדברי צח, רוב החברות שנרכשו היו רווחיות, ומתוך שבע רק אחת הייתה במצוקה.
claims.quote: Most of the companies we acquired were profitable. Out of our seven companies, only one was in distress.

claims.text: בנטוויץ' תואר כמנכ"ל של חברה ישראלית שבסיסה בתל אביב, שתשתמש בשותפויות האסטרטגיות להאצת פיתוח המוצר.
claims.quote: CropX CEO Isaac Bentwich said the Tel Aviv-based company plans to use the strategic partnerships to accelerate product development

claims.text: לדברי צח, ניסויים בארה"ב הראו שהמוצר חוסך 40% מהמים ומגדיל את היבול ב-10%.
claims.quote: We have shown that our product saves 40% of water and increases yield by 10%.

claims.text: לפי AgFunderNews, CropX רכשה את Tule Technologies בינואר 2023.
claims.quote: Tule Technologies (US) – Jan 2023 – Precision irrigation startup with above-canopy evapotranspiration measurement technology.

claims.text: לפי הראיון, החברה גייסה 11 מיליון דולר בסבב A וגייסת כעת סבב B.
claims.quote: The firm has raised $11 million in a Series A round and is now raising Series B.

claims.text: לפי אתר CropX עצמה, החברה נוסדה ב-2013 בניו זילנד.
claims.quote: CropX was founded in 2013 in New Zealand
